item.statement: Subadditivity of t^r (r<=1) shows splitting a feature over neurons never makes it cheaper
item.what_to_check: Standard l_p quasi-norm argument; possibly implicit in Morwani/representation-cost papers

chk.evidence:
The step in approach.tex l.64-67 is sum_j A_j^r <= sum_{i,j}|beta_ij|^r for r = b/nu <= 1. It uses subadditivity of t^r, which is the p-subadditivity (a+b)^p <= a^p + b^p that defines a p-norm for 0<p<=1. This is textbook material on quasi-Banach spaces; the canonical reference is Kalton-Peck-Roberts, An F-space Sampler, LMS LNS 89 (bibliographic data confirmed via abebooks; the book text was not read).

The ML version of the same argument is in Ongie & Parhi, arXiv 2606.14954. I fetched the PDF and grepped it:
- Def 3.5 defines a p-seminorm by Q(f+g)^p <= Q(f)^p + Q(g)^p.
- Prop 3.6: if K is absolutely p-homogeneous and subadditive, then K^{1/p} is a p-seminorm.
- Prop 3.13: parameter-level q-subadditivity makes the representation cost subadditive.
- Sec. 8, after eq. 8.30: "the subadditivity follows by concatenating neurons".
- Thm 9.3: for depth L>=2, R_L is a (2/L)-seminorm.

This is the statement "a merged feature costs no more than its split pieces" for weight-decay costs.

Gunasekar-Lee-Soudry-Srebro, arXiv 1806.00468, abstract fetched: depth-L linear conv nets go to "the l_{2/L} bridge penalty in the frequency domain". That is the closest precedent for a product parametrisation giving an l_{2/L} quasi-norm on Fourier coefficients.

Our contribution is not the inequality. It is using it so the universal bound holds with no hypothesis on neuron structure (mixing, interference, inactive neurons).

Searches: "l_p quasi-norm p<1 subadditivity p-normed space"; "representation cost weight decay splitting neuron subadditive l_{2/L} quasi-norm"; "Kalton Peck Roberts F-space sampler".

recommended_citations.why: Supports approach.tex l.67 ('splitting a feature over several neurons never makes it cheaper'). Prop 3.6/3.13 and Thm 9.3 show that weight-decay representation costs are subadditive, 'by concatenating neurons'. Their roots are p-seminorms, e.g. (2/L)-seminorms for depth L.

Precedent for a product-of-L-factors parametrisation inducing an l_{2/L} bridge (quasi-norm) penalty on Fourier-domain coefficients (abstract). It is the closest analog of pricing a frequency's amplitude A at A^{b/nu}. Venue is NeurIPS 2018; the arXiv page showed only the arXiv listing.

The textbook reference would be Kalton-Peck-Roberts 1984, An F-space Sampler; add it only if the bib entry is checked, since its bibliographic data was confirmed only through a retailer page. Do not present the technique as new.
